intro: The Mahabharata is often called the longest poem in the world. It tells of two branches of one royal family, the five Pandava brothers and their hundred Kaurava cousins, and the great war between them.

Inside the Mahabharata is the Bhagavad Gita, a conversation between the warrior Arjuna and Krishna, his charioteer. Many Hindus treasure it as one of their most important texts. The epic also holds many smaller stories, like Savitri and Nala.

By the end, you will be able to name the main people and events of the epic. You will be able to explain Krishna's key teaching in Gita 2.47. You will be able to show how different readers answer the epic's hard questions.
bigQuestion: What does the Mahabharata teach about doing what is right when every choice is hard?

timeline.t: Scholars think the Mahabharata grew between about 400 BCE and 400 CE
Adi Parva: the families are born; the Pandavas marry Draupadi
Sabha Parva: the dice game; the Pandavas lose everything
Vana Parva: twelve years in the forest; stories of Savitri and Nala
Virata Parva: one year in disguise
Bhishma Parva: the war begins; Krishna teaches Arjuna the Gita
The eighteen-day war and what comes after
K. T. Telang's English Gita appears in Sacred Books of the East
Swami Vivekananda speaks at the World's Parliament of Religions in Chicago

test.q: Whom does tradition credit with the Mahabharata?
How many parvas does the Mahabharata have?

test.why: The Kauravas are Dhritarashtra's hundred sons.

test.q: Which Pandava is the great archer?
What question does Draupadi ask in the hall?
choices: Could a man who lost himself still bet her?
test.why: In the Sabha Parva, Draupadi challenges the elders with this question.

test.q: What must the Pandavas do in their thirteenth year of exile?
test.why: They must stay hidden in disguise for one year.

test.q: Why does Karna fight against his brothers?
choices: He does not know how to fight
He stays loyal to his friend Duryodhana
test.why: Karna stays loyal to Duryodhana, who stood by him.

test.q: In which book is the Bhagavad Gita?
test.why: The Gita is in the Bhishma Parva.

test.q: Why does Arjuna set down his bow?
choices: He does not want to kill his relatives and teachers
test.why: Arjuna sees family and teachers on the other side.

choices: Do your duty without clinging to the reward
test.why: Gita 2.47 teaches action without clinging to results.

test.q: What does the Gita compare the body to?
Who wins her husband back from Yama?
test.why: Savitri wins Satyavan back from Yama.

test.q: Why is Nala's story told to Yudhishthira?
choices: To give him hope in exile
test.why: Nala also lost his kingdom at dice and later won it back.

test.q: What does the Mahabharata say about dharma?
choices: It is subtle, or hard to see

write.prompt: Was Arjuna right to be afraid to fight? Use Bhagavad Gita 1.28–32 (Arjuna's sorrow) and 2.47 (Krishna's answer), in Telang's translation (1882). Explain what the Gita says, and how two readers, such as a reader who sees a real war and Gandhi, have read it.
tips: Name the chapter and verse of each passage you use.
Write "the Gita says" or "Krishna tells Arjuna" when you report a teaching.
Show two readings side by side instead of judging one.
Use at least three words from this unit.
